claims.text: Keeping extraction (per-file, expensive, parallelizable) apart from resolution (whole-repo, cheap, serial) is what lets the parse run in a worker process while resolution stays in the parent.
claims.why: The chunk does not show any worker process or parent/child split; claim about architecture cannot be verified from this code.

claims.text: Handles both absolute (``from daedalus.core import x``) and RELATIVE (``from .router import x``, ``from ..core import y``) imports — the latter anchored to ``src_dotted`` (this file's own dotted module), which is essential inside packages that use relative imports heavily.
claims.why: Code includes logic for level>0 (relative) and level==0 (absolute) imports, using src_dotted to construct base module.

claims.text: Annotations are captured as RAW TEXT and never resolved here. Under ``from __future__ import annotations`` an annotation may be written as a string, and that is the NORMAL case in this repo; ``annotation_text`` folds the quoted and unquoted spellings onto the same text, so a consumer never has to care which one the author used.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain function annotation_text or any code capturing annotations; claim refers to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: Nothing here imports anything from the analysed source: ``typing.get_type_hints`` would EXECUTE imports, which is an egress/safety violation in this codebase.
claims.why: No imports from analysed source are shown; claim about get_type_hints not present in chunk.

claims.text: A bare ``Any`` must never become an edge target (it is the explicit ABSENCE of type information, and as a node it would be a hub that poisons every ranking), so ``normalize_annotation`` reports it as the ``is_any`` flag with an EMPTY member list -- refusing to edge is the safe default, not an opt-in.
claims.why: Chunk does not contain normalize_annotation function; claim about its behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: This constant is the label to count it under. It is not a legal Python identifier, so it cannot be mistaken for a type name if it ever does reach an id.
claims.why: ANY_SENTINEL is defined as '<any>', which contains angle brackets and is not a valid Python identifier.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT field-compatible with ``CodeUnit``: no ``source``, no ``loc``. That is the enforcement of 'type is a forest node, never a unit' (see the section header). ``markdown.DocSection`` made the OPPOSITE choice on purpose, because a doc section is meant to reach ``build_resolver``.
claims.why: Chunk does not contain CodeUnit or markdown.DocSection definitions; compatibility claim cannot be checked.

observations.what: Function _import_records has type annotation 'out: list[tuple]' but tuple is not subscriptable in Python <3.9; uses 'tuple' without importing from typing.
resolve_python_imports uses 'src_dotted' with default empty string; relative imports with empty src_dotted may produce incorrect module paths.
TypeDecl is frozen dataclass but fields are not annotated with types (e.g., module: str).
Comment states 'Bump when the MEANING of any record below changes' but no enforcement mechanism is present.
